name: Low-dose gemcitabine radiosensitizer with concurrent radiation (bladder trimodality)
cyclesNote: Low-dose gemcitabine as a radiosensitizer given weekly (or twice weekly) through the external-beam radiation course of bladder-preserving trimodality therapy; number of doses tracks the radiation schedule.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: Low-dose gemcitabine is a cisplatin-free radiosensitizing option during bladder-preserving trimodality therapy, an alternative when cisplatin is unsuitable.

supportiveCare: Deliver gemcitabine on radiation-treatment days; coordinate timing with radiation.
Monitor for myelosuppression and radiation cystitis/proctitis.
Restaging cystoscopy + biopsy after chemoradiation; salvage cystectomy for non-response.
monitoring: radiation cystitis / proctitis during the course

doseModificationRules.text: Hold or reduce gemcitabine for myelosuppression; radiation generally continues. Physician decides.

drugs.name: gemcitabine
drugs.notes: Low-dose gemcitabine 27 mg/m2 IV twice weekly as a radiosensitizer during RT. An alternative schedule is gemcitabine about 100 mg/m2 IV once weekly during RT. Radiosensitizing doses are far below systemic chemotherapy dosing. Own wording; standard reference dose.

provenance.locator: Principles of bladder preservation - low-dose gemcitabine radiosensitization
